title: Pilot pathway owner ledger
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, tactical tracker for pilot -> production rollouts that focuses on owner accountability, near-term blockers, and actions that materially affect renewal signal. Use during daily standups and pre-QBR prep.

How to use:
- One row per milestone / gate. Keep rows concise.
- Owner = single point of contact responsible for planning + updates (does not imply solo execution).
- Status = green / yellow / red (notes explaining why).
- Blockers should map to a mitigation owner + ETA. If blocker requires escalation, mark Escalate:true and ping escalation owner.
- Move items right as they progress; keep previous notes under "history" bullets.

Snapshot (as of 2026-02-20):
Milestone | Owner | Target ETA | Status | Primary Blocker(s) | Mitigation + ETA | Notes / History
1) Contract signature (SOW signed) | Maya Bennett | 2025-11-18 | green | N/A | N/A | Contract signed; billing onboarding scheduled 11/20
2) Network & VPN provisioning | Diego Morales | 2025-11-25 | yellow | Customer firewall policy review (pending) | Diego to run FW rule template; customer SOC to review by 2025-11-30 | Waiting on SOC availability; escalated to customer GTM lead 11/24
3) Private control plane deployment (v0.9) | Samir Rao | 2025-12-08 | yellow | Image signing and internal cert chain mismatch | Samir to coordinate SRE patch and reimage by 2025-12-04 | See runbook section for cert workaround used in Acme rollout (confluence link)
4) Model onboarding (3x models) | Claire Zhang | 2025-12-15 | red | Model conversion failing on quantized path (OOM) | Claire + AppliedML to test 4-bit conversion; fallback to FP16 until root cause fixed by 2025-12-12 | Customer evaluating accuracy delta between FP16 and 4-bit; potential cost delta flagged for renewal conversation
5) Canary traffic test (1% of prod) | Asha Patel | 2026-01-10 | yellow | Autoscaling policy not triggering under synthetic load | Asha to simulate observed traffic pattern and adjust scaling window by 2025-12-20 | Will validate with SLO breach test 12/29
6) Performance SLO verification (p95 latency) | Samir Rao | 2026-01-15 | yellow | KV cache miss rate higher than expected | Tune cache TTLs; add prefix cache for repeat requests by 2026-01-04 | Need additional request traces (see linked artifact: JIRA-4389)
7) Training + Prompt tuning handoff | Claire Zhang | 2026-01-21 | green | N/A | N/A | Customer provided labeled set v1, training scheduled 1/07
8) Production cutover | Customer PM (Alex Kim) | 2026-02-01 | red | Billing integration and usage quotas discrepancy | Finance to confirm billing SKU mapping by 2026-01-20; CS to freeze pre-cutover usage at limit | Escalation flagged: Finance-Lead (Priya S.) contacted 2026-01-12

Risk register (short):
- Model quantization risk: high impact on cost but could degrade accuracy. Current mitigation: temporarily serve FP16 variants and run A/B evals on 2k example prompts. Owner: Claire.
- Network window: customer SOC availability is a critical path. Secondary mitigation: offer short-lived bastion access for initial validation. Owner: Diego.
- Billing mapping: mismatch could block cutover and impact renewal. Owner: Maya + Finance. Escalation: Priya S.

Escalation path & SLA expectations:
- Level 1 (CS Lead): Maya Bennett — 24 hour response for blockers marked yellow
- Level 2 (CS Head): Priya Sharma — 8 hour response for red blockers affecting go-live
- Level 3 (Product/Eng Pager): Samir Rao (serving runtime) / Diego Morales (network) — 4 hour acknowledgement for infra blocking items

Pre-QBR data pull checklist (owner in parentheses):
- Top 5 customer-facing incidents (Maya)
- Usage by model & token spend last 30d (Finance, Maya)
- SLO compliance last 30d (Samir)
- Accuracy/regression report vs baseline (Claire)
- Renewal health snapshot & risk tier (Asha)

Renewal health snapshot (qualitative):
- Consumption: Moderate (ramped quickly in first 2 weeks, then plateau)
- Technical risk: Medium-High (quantization + network windows remain unresolved)
- Exec sentiment: Neutral-Positive — PM engaged but execs expect cutover by Feb to hit internal timelines
- Recommended QBR asks: commit to a cutover date window, share cost delta for FP16 vs 4-bit options, confirm SOC signoff cadence

Open actions (next 7 days):
- Claire: finish 4-bit conversion experiments and post accuracy matrix (due 2025-12-04)
- Samir: patch cert chain and re-run private control plane validation (due 2025-12-04)
- Diego: provide firewall rule template + schedule SOC review (due 2025-11-30)
- Maya: align billing SKU mapping with Finance and get signoff (due 2025-11-20)
- Asha: prepare QBR slide stub focused on technical blockers and renewal ask (due 2025-12-01)

Notes to self / team (informal):
- If the quantization work drags >2 weeks, propose a managed FP16 tier for first 3 months with a cost-sharing pilot to reduce perceived risk.
- Keep a running short list of 10 canonical prompts to use for regression checks — low friction to run and share in QBR.
- When raising escalation, include: reproducer, timestamped logs, minimal diffs, and suggested mitigations. Saves cycles.

History & decisions (short):
- 2025-11-01: Initial kickoff call; customer committed to pilot in Nov.
- 2025-11-10: Agreed to 3-model onboarding scope and private control plane option.
- 2025-11-18: Contract signed. Decided to split quantization rollout from canary to avoid blocking cutover.

Appendix: useful links and runbooks
- Private deploy runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Infra/Private+Deploy+Runbook
- Quantization troubleshooting notes (Claire): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AML/Quant+Notes
- Billing SKU matrix (Finance): https://sheets.redwood.ai/spreadsheets/d/Billing-SKU-Matrix

Last update notes (2026-02-20):
- Updated milestone target ETAs after weekly sync.
- Added explicit escalation owner for billing.
- Marked model conversion issue as high priority for the next sprint.

Editors: Asha (owner), Claire (tech lead), Maya (CS lead).

-- end of doc --
